nodes.description: B-cell lymphoma in adulthood in both affected members of the founding G159R family. Together with the chronic lymphocytic leukaemia of the N160S family this makes B-cell malignancy a feature of both allele groups rather than of one, and Aiolos-deficient mice develop B-cell lymphomas with age, which is the model-organism counterpart. The denominators are two small families, so the magnitude of the predisposition is unknown.

nodes.description: The step every reported allele shares. Mutant-containing complexes fail to bind the canonical AIOLOS-IKAROS motif and fail pericentromeric heterochromatin targeting, and the damage is done through dimerization rather than through loss of AIOLOS dosage: removing the mutant's dimerization capacity restores B-cell development. This node deliberately does not assert that wild-type IKAROS is corrupted, because that holds for G159R and not for N160S; the IKAROS arm is a separate, allele-scoped node.

nodes.description: Allele-specific to G159R. Mutant AIOLOS sequesters wild-type IKAROS into complexes that bind neither canonical motif and are redirected to genomic regions lacking both, so one mutant allele of IKZF3 disables the product of a second, unmutated gene. The AIOLOS-associated inborn-error review states the asymmetry directly: G159R acts against AIOLOS and IKAROS, while N160S acts exclusively against AIOLOS. This is the node the founding report's heterodimeric interference names, and scoping it to one allele is what the sources support.

Allele-specific to N160S. In the N160S knock-in mouse the early B-cell developmental block seen with G159R is absent, and the distinguishing abnormality is impaired induction of CD62L in lymphocytes with defective homing to lymph nodes. The review attributes this to IKAROS dysfunction, which sits awkwardly beside its own finding that N160S does not act dominant-negatively against IKAROS in the targeting assay; the entry records the observation and the attribution separately rather than resolving a tension the sources leave open.
